title: Covenants
hook: Covenants traces six great promises from a garden to an upper room—each one Promise, Person, and Prayer—until Scripture stops being a pile of books and becomes one unfolding story.

body.text: You believe God keeps His promises. You have always believed it. But underneath that belief there is often a quieter, more exhausting one — a nagging sense that His goodwill toward you is somehow riding on your performance, that the promise is real but perhaps not quite meant for you, that if you prayed harder, believed better, failed less, then maybe the blessing would finally come. It is an exhausting way to live, and it is not the good news.

It is night in the land of Canaan. A childless old man asks God a very human question: How can I know? And God does not answer with an argument. He tells the man to cut animals in two and lay the halves opposite each other. Then, as a deep sleep falls, the man watches God Himself — veiled in fire — pass alone between the pieces. Both parties were meant to walk that aisle. Only One does, taking the entire oath, and the entire curse for breaking it, onto Himself, while the man it was sworn to lies unconscious in the dark.

That is what a covenant is — not a contract, but a promise sealed in blood. In six unhurried chapters, Covenants walks the six great promises that hold up the whole of Scripture, from a garden to an upper room — each one Promise, Person, and Prayer — until the many separate books stop being a pile and become a single, unfolding story.
From a curse overheard in a garden to a cup lifted at a table. From a rainbow hung in judgment to a throne death could not empty.

title: Burning Hearts
hook: Two men walked seven miles carrying grief. A stranger opened the Scriptures, and their hearts caught fire.

body.text: Did Not Our Hearts Burn?

You open it faithfully enough — a chapter before the day starts, a psalm before the light goes out — and you close it again feeling much the same as when you began. If that’s familiar, you’re in good company. We believe this Book. We want it to move us. But too often it reads like a stranger’s voice: old, dignified, a little remote.

Two men walked seven miles out of Jerusalem on the first Easter afternoon carrying the three saddest words in all of Scripture — we had hoped. A stranger fell into step beside them and opened the Scriptures, and something caught fire in them long before they knew who He was. By nightfall they were running the whole road back in the dark.
That is the claim this book rests on: what the risen Christ did for two grieving travelers through the same pages, He still means to do for anyone who will walk a while and listen.

In six warm, unhurried chapters, Burning Hearts follows those two men one part at a time — their hearts, their ears, their eyes, their hands, their feet, their lips — and traces the journey the Word makes through any life that lets it in.
From a buried hope to a story told. From a whisper of grief to a shout of joy.

title: The Power of Prayer
hook: Most believers pray. Few have discovered how.

body.text: Most of us know how to pray. Fewer of us know how to pray with authority, persistence, and power — or why some prayers seem to change everything while others bounce off the ceiling and fall back to the floor.

The Power of Prayer opens up what most believers have only partially received: a vision of prayer not as a single activity but as a complete way of life. Drawing on twelve dimensions — from the authority seated with Christ that grounds every request, to mountain-moving faith, intercession, fasting, spiritual warfare, prophetic hearing, and worship — Aneel Aranha shows how these expressions of prayer fit together into one integrated life with God.

This is not a book about praying harder but about praying differently — from a position of rest rather than striving, from confidence rather than hesitation, and from a relationship already established rather than one you are still trying to earn.
For the believer who has walked away from prayer wondering whether anything happened — and for anyone ready to discover what can — this is the invitation.

title: Praying the Scriptures
hook: When you run out of things to say to God, Praying the Scriptures shows you how to let Scripture pray for you.

body.text: You begin well enough — you thank God, name the people you love, mention what’s weighing on you — and then, around the third minute, you hit an awkward silence. If that’s familiar, you’re in good company. We love God. We want to pray. But prayer so often feels thin, repetitive, and improvised.

This book is about a discovery that changes all of that. We already hold the richest language of prayer ever written, and most of us have never thought to use it. The Bible is not only a book to be read. It is a book to be prayed.
The psalmists, the prophets, the apostles, and Jesus Himself all took the words God had spoken and offered them back to Him — and when they did, heaven moved.

In six warm, practical chapters, Praying the Scriptures hands you a simple, repeatable way to do the same: pray the Psalms, plead God’s promises, intercede with Paul’s prayers over the people you love, find words for the dark seasons, and speak Scripture together with one voice.
The goal isn’t information. It’s a transformed life of prayer.
The Bible becomes your prayer book. His promises become your requests. His Word becomes your voice.

title: The School of Discipleship – Phase 1
subtitle: Arise
hook: Phase I of the School of Discipleship, ARISE moves through five modules — Awaken, Receive, Integrate, Strengthen, Engage — for a life reshaped from within.

body.text: Something in you knows there is more.

More than Sunday services and scattered devotions. More than believing the right things without becoming a different person. You were created for a life of genuine transformation — and there is a clear path to get there.

ARISE is Phase I of the School of Discipleship — a proven framework for Christian formation built on the discipleship model Jesus Himself established. Through five progressive modules, ARISE takes you on a complete journey:
Awaken — discover what God did through salvation and who you truly are in Christ.
Receive — encounter the Holy Spirit and learn to walk daily in His power.
Integrate — practice the spiritual disciplines that reshape your character from the inside out.
Strengthen — build the habits of prayer and Scripture that sustain lifelong growth.
Engage — step into stewardship, service, witness, and Kingdom impact.
Whether you are taking your first steps with Jesus or wondering why the journey feels stalled, ARISE meets you where you are and takes you where God is calling you to be.
Twenty sessions. One complete journey. A life transformed from the inside out.
The book is available in Kindle, paperback and hardcover editions worldwide on Amazon. In India it is available on pothi.com.

title: Why Jesus Came to Die
subtitle: 40 Reasons
hook: One cross, forty reasons. A slow, reflective journey through everything Christ accomplished at Calvary — more than you ever imagined.

body.text: Most Christians know one reason Jesus came to die.
This book will show you forty.

Why Jesus Came to Die takes you deeper — through forty reasons, forty distinct purposes, forty facets of what Christ accomplished at Calvary. Jesus died to absorb the wrath of God, to cancel every charge against us, to reconcile us to God, to give us access to His presence, and — on the last of these forty reflections — to ensure that the moment your eyes close for the final time, they open again in His.

Each chapter is designed to be read slowly, reflected upon, and prayed through. Together, they form a portrait of the cross that is more vast, more personal, and more wondrous than most of us have ever imagined.

Aneel Aranha and Kiran Joseph are preachers and ministry partners who have devoted themselves to helping ordinary people encounter extraordinary truth. These forty reflections began as a Lenten preaching series and grew into the book you are holding — their most sustained and personal exploration of the heart of the Christian faith.
The cross changed everything. This book will help you see how.

title: God Sees
subtitle: Finding Hope When You Feel Invisible
hook: Hagar named Him “the God who sees me.” Five overlooked figures in Scripture answer the question you’ve never said out loud.

body.text: Does God see me?

It is a quiet question. It rarely announces itself. But it sits beneath the surface of countless faithful lives — people who pray, who serve, who show up week after week, yet carry a persistent doubt that God is truly paying attention to them. Not to humanity in general. To them.

God Sees is a pastoral answer to that doubt. Through five figures of Scripture who each knew what it meant to feel overlooked — Hagar abandoned in the wilderness, David hiding in a cave, Hannah weeping in silence, a single sparrow no one would think to count, and Joseph forgotten in a prison cell — this book traces one steady truth: the God of the Bible sees you, knows you, hears you, values you, and remembers you.

The first person in all of Scripture to give God a name was not a patriarch or a prophet, but a desperate slave woman who discovered she was not invisible after all. She called Him El Roi — the God who sees me.
If you have ever wondered whether He sees you, these pages were written for you.
You are not invisible to Him. You never have been. And you never will be.

title: Scripture in Action
subtitle: Volume 1
hook: Reading the Bible is good. Living it is transformational. Discover the five-step system turning Scripture into daily action.

body.text: Reading the Bible in a year is good.
Living it out daily is transformational.
Most Bible reading plans focus on information. This one focuses on transformation.
You’ve felt it—the gap between reading Scripture and actually living it. Between knowing God’s Word and experiencing its power in your everyday decisions, relationships, and challenges.
Scripture in Action bridges that gap with a revolutionary approach that combines Old Testament wisdom, New Testament truth, and practical daily application in ways that will surprise you.
This isn’t just another Bible reading plan. It’s a life-change system:
260 weekday readings designed for busy lives with intentional rest
Thematic connections that illuminate God’s character across testaments
Five daily action steps that move Scripture from your head to your hands
Reflection questions that dig deeper than surface-level reading
Prayer points that turn study into conversation with God

Thousands are already experiencing this approach through the daily podcast. They’re discovering that when you put Scripture into action, it doesn’t just change your Bible reading—it changes everything.
The question isn’t whether God’s Word has power. The question is whether you’ll unleash that power in your daily life.
Your transformation through Scripture begins now.

title: Practicing God’s Presence
hook: You don’t need a quieter life to meet God—you need to wake up to the life you already have.

body.text: You don’t need to escape your life to find God
—you need to find God in your life.
Most of us think spiritual growth happens in the quiet moments—early morning prayer, Sunday worship, annual retreats. But what about the other 165 hours of our week?

In the 1600s, a French monk named Brother Lawrence discovered something revolutionary: he learned to experience God’s presence not just in the chapel, but while washing dishes, mending shoes, and doing the mundane tasks of monastery life. His simple practice transformed not only his own spiritual life but has inspired seekers for over three centuries.

Practicing God’s Presence brings Brother Lawrence’s ancient wisdom into the rhythms of modern life. Through honest personal stories, biblical insight, and practical guidance, Aneel Aranha shows how ordinary Christians can cultivate continuous awareness of God—not by adding more spiritual activities to an already packed schedule, but by learning to recognize God in the life we’re already living.

This isn’t a book about becoming more religious. It’s about becoming more awake to the God who is already with you—in traffic, at work, during conflict, in joy and suffering, through the mundane and the magnificent.

Whether you’re exhausted by trying harder, frustrated by spiritual dryness, or simply longing for more of God in your everyday experience, this book offers a way forward. Not through guilt or performance, but through a practice so simple a kitchen monk perfected it while peeling potatoes.
Your life doesn’t need to change for you to experience God. You just need to wake up to the life you already have.
Includes selected writings from The Practice of the Presence of God by Brother Lawrence.

title: Making All Things New
subtitle: From Brokenness to Healing
hook: What if your broken pieces are exactly what God wants to use? Nineteen sermons that map the way forward.

body.text: What if the broken pieces of your life are exactly what God wants to use?

In Making All Things New, you’ll discover that God doesn’t wait for you to get your act together before He begins His work. He meets you in the mess, the failure, the crisis, the chains you can’t break on your own. Through nineteen powerful messages organized into four life-changing movements, this book maps the journey from spiritual spectator to transformed disciple:
New Beginnings shows how God transforms crisis into crown and failure into faith—revealing that your worst moments may become your greatest testimonies.
Spiritual Disciplines explores the spiritual practices that deepen faith, from praying dangerous prayers to embracing doubt as a pathway to stronger belief.
Grace and Truth introduces you to a Jesus you may have never met—one who offers scandalous grace and embodies the perfect dance between truth and love.
Kingdom Living challenges you to move from personal transformation to communal impact, becoming a peacemaker and bridge builder in a divided world.

Born from six months of Spirit-led preaching that transformed an entire congregation, these messages aren’t theoretical—they’re testimonies. They’re not religious platitudes—they’re proven pathways. Each chapter ends with practical reflections to help you apply these truths to your own journey.

Whether you’re struggling with addiction, shame, or fear; seeking deeper spiritual growth; or longing to see God unite His divided people, this book offers hope grounded in lived experience and biblical truth.
The God who made all things is ready to make all things new in your life—starting with you.

title: ARISE
subtitle: A Blueprint for Revival in Our Time
hook: Revival isn’t coming—it’s here. Five steps that move you from spiritual spectator to revival catalyst.

body.text: The revival we’ve been praying for isn’t coming—it’s here!
But most of us don’t know how to position ourselves to be part of it.
In a world fractured by division, paralyzed by fear, and desperate for authentic transformation, God is calling His people to arise. Not tomorrow. Not when we’re ready. Now.

Drawing from a powerful season of preaching that transformed his own congregation, Aneel Aranha discovered a divine blueprint hidden in plain sight—five essential steps that move us from spiritual spectators to revival catalysts:
Know Who You Are – Discover your true identity in Christ
See with New Eyes – Develop resurrection vision for impossible situations
Imagine God’s Possibilities – Partner with the Divine Dreamer
Embody Truth and Grace – Master the dance that transforms relationships
Unite the Church – Become a bridge builder in a divided world
This isn’t theory. It’s field-tested truth already igniting transformation in churches and communities worldwide. Each chapter combines biblical depth with practical steps you can take today.
The question isn’t whether God wants to bring revival. The question is whether you’ll become the kind of person through whom He can bring it.
Your part in God’s great awakening begins now.

title: The Blessed Lamb of God
subtitle: Discovering Your True Identity in Christ
hook: I am redeemed. I am saved. I am restored. Sixteen truths that reveal who you really are in Christ.

body.text: What if you’ve been living far below your spiritual privileges as a child of God?

Born from a divine encounter and crystallized in a song touching hearts worldwide, “The Blessed Lamb of God” explores sixteen powerful biblical declarations that reveal who you truly are in Christ: “I am redeemed… I am saved… I am restored…”

Through compelling stories and biblical insights, Aneel Aranha shows how understanding your true identity in Christ changes everything—from handling failure to relating with others. Whether struggling with guilt, feeling spiritually defeated, or wanting to live more fully in God’s purposes, this book anchors you in the unshakeable truth of who you are because of what Christ has done.

Each chapter includes Scripture focus, practical exercises, and reflection questions to help you live these truths experientially. Discover the freedom of knowing you are God’s beloved child, Jesus’ friend, and the Holy Spirit’s dwelling place.
Stop surviving spiritually and start thriving in the abundant life Christ purchased for you.
Perfect for individual study, small groups, or anyone seeking to understand their place in God’s family.

title: Divine Appointments
subtitle: A Christian’s Guide to Sharing Jesus
hook: Uncertain, afraid of offense, worried about the friendship? A practical guide to sharing Christ across the faith divide.

body.text: A Practical Guide for Meaningful Dialogue

Have you ever hesitated to share your faith with a Muslim friend? Whether it’s uncertainty about Islamic beliefs, fear of causing offense, or concern about damaging valued relationships, many Christians struggle to bridge this faith divide.

Divine Appointments provides clear, practical guidance for sharing Jesus with Muslim friends. Drawing from decades of experience, Aneel Aranha deftly navigates the theological, cultural, and personal challenges that often arise. Through real-life examples and actionable advice, you’ll learn how to:
Build genuine friendships across faith boundaries
Answer common questions about Christianity with grace and wisdom
Navigate cultural sensitivities while staying true to your faith
Recognize and respond to divine opportunities for spiritual conversations

This comprehensive guide helps you move beyond fear and uncertainty to share Christ’s love effectively with your Muslim friends. Whether you’re just beginning to build relationships with Muslims or have years of experience, Divine Appointments will equip you with the knowledge and confidence to share your faith with wisdom and grace.
“A must-read for anyone seeking to share Christ’s love with Muslim friends. Practical, sensitive, and deeply insightful.”

title: The Seven Deadly Sins
hook: Pride, envy, lust, sloth—ancient vices wearing digital disguises. A guide to breaking their grip and finding freedom.

body.text: Breaking Free in a Digital World

In this compelling exploration of Christianity’s seven deadly sins – pride, avarice, envy, anger, lust, gluttony, and sloth – author Aneel Aranha reveals how these ancient vices manifest in our modern world, particularly in our digital age.
Through biblical wisdom, contemporary examples, and practical guidance, the author shows how these sins can poison our spiritual lives at their very root.

Yet this book offers more than mere warning – it provides a transformative pathway toward their corresponding virtues: humility, generosity, kindness, patience, chastity, temperance, and diligence. Whether you’re struggling with these age-old temptations or seeking deeper spiritual growth, The Seven Deadly Sins offers timeless wisdom for the contemporary Christian journey.
